goals.title: From beach stones to an electric cart
goals.pitch: Lumi builds an electric cart from nothing but what the island has: copper smelted from green rock, wire pulled through a stone plate, cells of two metals in sea water, a motor wound and fitted part by part. The cart drives the friends round the island because every part works, and nothing is scripted.
goals.play: Gather, smelt, draw, wind, fit, switch on, and the one field-and-circuit solver decides what happens. More turns give more torque, thin wire glows and melts, a magnet put in the wrong way round drives the rotor backwards, too few cells and the cart crawls up the hill, a loose brush makes it stutter. Every build is different because the player chooses the parts, their sizes and materials and where they sit. Then the cart gets better the way real ones did: a gear pair for the hill, a second motor, a switch to reverse, a hill run that charges the cells as it brakes.
goals.moment: The first cart, all wooden frame and copper coils, coughs, lurches forward with three friends on board, crawls up the dune and runs away down the other side. Or a misbuilt motor spins its own rotor out of the frame and the friends scatter.
road: Done s146-151: any magnet's field (em.jl), the homopolar wire motor, coil Biot-Savart (coilcrane.jl), the beach magnet stone
A circuit solver from what touches what: wires, contacts, resistance from length and section, Joule heat
A cell from copper and iron in a clam shell of sea water: voltage, internal resistance, polarisation
The coil crane powered by cells: more cells lift more spikes
A motor fitted by hand: stator stone, wound rotor on an axle, split-ring commutator, brushes; torque only from the field solve
The motor on the potter's wheel: it turns by itself; turned by hand it is a generator that lights a wire
Wheels, axle and a wooden frame as rigid bodies with rolling contact on the terrain
The cart: cells and motor on the frame, a switch in Lumi's beak; it drives because the parts do
Gears for the hill, reverse, braking that charges the cells; friends ride along
Copper from green rock in the kiln, drawn into wire, so every part is made on the island
